lectures.title: Time and Space Complexity of Singly Linked List

cues.en: Now, in the last lecture of this section, I'm just going to combine all the methods that we have created
together to see the time and space complexity of single linked list.
Now, when we are creating a single linked list, the time complexity will be o one and the space complexity
also will be o one.
Because the constructor function runs in a constant time and space as it is simply setting values.
Now the next method is append method.
Appending to the end of the linked list is a constant time operation, because we maintain a tail pointer,
and the space complexity is also o one.
The next method is prepend method, so prepending to the linked list is a constant operation because
it involves setting a few pointers, and the space complexity is also o one.
Now, when it comes to the.
Inserting, the time complexity for this method is going to be on because in the worst case, it has
to traverse the entire single linked list.
The space complexity is o one because we are only creating a single new node using a temporary pointer.
Then we have a search method.
The search method takes o n time complexity in the worst case, because we have to visit all nodes in
the single linked list.
So the space complexity is o one because it uses a single temporary pointer.
Then we have a traverse method.
So traverse method will traverse all elements of the single linked list.
So that's why the time complexity is o n and the space complexity is O one.
Then we have a get method.
So the get method will take o n time complexity because it may need to traverse entire the single linked
list to find the element.
And the space complexity is O one because it uses a temporary pointer.
Then we have set method.
So we learned that in the set method we are using the get method.
So the get method takes on time complexity.
So the set method also will take on time complexity.
So here again the space complexity is O one.
Then we have pop first method popping the first node is a constant operation as it is involving setting
a few pointers, and space complexity is also o one.
So for pop first method space and time complexity is o one.
Now for pop method, which is popping the element from the end of the linked list is going to be on,
because we have to traverse the entire list to find the second last node.
The space complexity is o one because here we are just using temporary pointer.
Remove method also takes all n time complexity, because here we are going to traverse the through the
list to find out the node that we want to delete.
So in the worst case it's going to be o n and the space complexity is o one.
Now when it comes to deleting all nodes, the time and space complexity is o one, because we are just
setting the head and tail pointers to none, and we are just setting the length to zero.
So that's why the space and time complexity is going to be o one.
So with this we have come to the end of this section.
So in this section we have covered all details of single linked list and hopefully everything is clear.
